headline: Approved a police budget amendment for 2026-2027 and two interdepartmental budget transfers for 2025-2026.
summary: Two members of the public spoke during public input. A proposed CBiz contract amendment for expanded audit services was added to the agenda and will be reviewed at a special meeting on Thursday. The lease modification for Laurel View Golf Course remains in progress, and the police chief reported that two cold case homicides were solved.
decisions: Approved the consent calendar, which includes two interdepartmental budget transfers for 2025-2026, 13 in favor and 0 opposed.
Approved amending the 2026-2027 fiscal year budget for police, 13 in favor and 0 opposed.

plain_text:
TOWN OF HAMDEN, 
CONNECTICUT 
 
LEGISLATIVE COUNCIL 
REGULAR MEETING 
  
AUGUST 10, 2026 
MINUTES DRAFT 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Present - Jeron Alston 
Present - Bob Anthony, Min. Leader 
 Present - Sean Cardwell, Pro Tem 
 Present - Rhonda Caldwell 
Present - Maurine Crouch 
Present - Tom Figlar, Min. Whip 
Present - Doug Foley 
Present - Sarah Gallagher, Maj. Leader 
Present - Tasha Hunt, Maj. Whip 
Present - Abdul Osmanu 
Present - Tameeka Parks 
Absent - Ted Stevens 
Present - Grace Teodosio 
 Present - Adrian Webber 
Present - Katie Kiely, President  
1. CALL OF THE MEETING AND TAKING OF THE ROLL 
Legislative Council Regular Meeting, August 10, 2026.  The meeting was called to order 
at 7:04pm with the members noted above in attendance Council member Stevens was 
absent.  
  
2. PUBLIC INPUT SESSION 
Public Input was opened at 7:10pm.  Two members of the public came forward to provide 
comments.  There were no written public comments received for tonight’s meeting.  The 
Public Input session was closed at 7:15pm.   
3. CORRESPONDENCE 
There was no written correspondence received for this meeting.  Council President Kiely 
reported that correspondence received last week had been forwarded to the 
administration for a response  
 
President Kiely requested that the agenda be amended to add an item regarding the 
proposed CBiz contract amendment for an expanded scope of audit services so it could 
be referred to the Committee of the Whole for consideration at a special meeting.  
Motion: Gallagher 
Second: Figlar  
Vote: 14 in favor, the motion to amend passed unanimously. 
 
With agreement on availability from the Council members, President Kiely announced a 
special meeting of the Committee of the Whole would be held on Thursday, August 13, 
2026.  
4.   RECESS 
      President Kiely recessed the Legislative Council at 7:22pm to convene the committees. 
 
Administration and Settlement Committee 
Engineering, Development & Municipal Planning Committee
Finance Committee 
Human Services Committee – not convened this evening 
IT & Civic Engagement Committee 
Public Safety Committee – not convened this evening 
Public Works, Facilities, and Sustainability Committee 
 
       President Kiely reconvened Legislative Council meeting at 9:24pm.  Roll call was 
       taken and all Councilors present as noted above were present. 
 
5.   COUNCIL PRESIDENT'S UPDATE 
1. News and Announcements 
2. Celebrations 
3. Legislative Council Committee Updates 
 
President Kiely recognized Police Chief Reynolds, who announced that the Hamden Police 
Department had successfully solved two cold case homicides through collaborative 
investigations with federal, state, and local law enforcement partners. Chief Reynolds also 
highlighted the success of the Town's National Night Out event and thanked the Council, 
Administration, Public Safety Committee, and members of the Hamden Police Department for 
their support. 
 
President Kiely then announced that a Special Committee of the Whole meeting and Special 
Legislative Council meeting would be held on Thursday at 8:00 p.m. to review the proposed 
CBiz contract amendment. She also recognized Director Bivens, her staff, and community 
partners for a successful summer camp program and thanked the Library Director for providing 
departmental updates to assist the Council in tracking programs and preparing for future 
budget discussions. 
 
President Kiely further announced that the Finance Commission would provide a report at the 
next regular Council meeting and noted that Attorney Steve Mednick would participate in 
upcoming leadership and Council meetings while preparations continued for a future special 
meeting to review proposed Rules updates. 
 
 
6.   REPORTS OF DEPARTMENTS, BOARDS, AND COMMISSIONS 
President Kiely reported that, as previously announced, the School Building Committee had 
been reconvened and that its first meeting was anticipated to be held in September. She noted 
that updates and meeting information would be provided once available. 
 
7. REPORTS OF COUNCIL LIASONS 
None provided this evening. 
 
8. EXECUTIVE SESSION  
Not required this evening.  
  
9. CONSENT CALENDAR  
  1. ORDER AUTHORIZING INTERDEPARTMENTAL TRANSFER 2025 - 2026 FISCAL 
YEAR BUDGET – TOWN ATTORNEY
2. ORDER AUTHORIZING INTERDEPARTMENTAL TRANSFER 2025 - 2026 FISCAL 
YEAR BUDGET – FINANCE – PURCHASING DIVISION 
 
President Kiely called for a motion to approve the Consent Calendar: 
Motion: Gallagher 
Second: Figlar  
Vote: 13 in favor, 0 opposed, 0 abstentions.  (Minority Leader Anthony stepped out 
and did not take part in the vote.)  
10. REGULAR AGENDA  
  1. ORDER AMENDING THE 2026-2027 FISCAL YEAR BUDGET (POLICE) 
President Kiely called for a motion to approve the Order. 
Motion: Cardwell 
Second: Gallagher   
Vote: 13 in favor, 0 opposed, 0 abstentions.  Item passed unanimously.  
  
11. UNFINISHED BUSINESS  
  1. ORDER AUTHORIZING THE MAYOR TO EXECUTE A LEASE MODIFICATION 
FOR LAUREL VIEW GOLF COURSE 
 
President Kiely reported that the Unfinished Business item remained in progress 
and that the Administration was actively working on the matter. She noted that 
discussions and communications with the parties involved were ongoing and that 
updates would be provided as additional information became available. 
  
12. NEW BUSINESS 
None 
  
13. ADJOURN 
There being no further business, President Kiely called for a motion to adjourn: 
Motion: Figlar 
Second: Gallagher 
 
The meeting adjourned at 9:42 p.m.
